_purpose: T091 (SpecKit-004 'fast-dev-cycles', User Story 3) golden-bad case for closure/reopen_rate.py (plan.md T-D06, tasks.md T100, contract cycle-time-report-cli.md CT-006). Reproduces, as a small synthetic isomorph, the EXACT population-mismatch class research/R1_baseline_cycle_time.md's Table D caveat names for the real tracker DB (whole-history reopen count 18 Bug items vs whole-history closed-count 31 Bug items with a closure event ever -- 'so "18 of 31 bugs" (58%) is an UPPER-BOUND-style ratio with mismatched populations (reopened items may have been closed before item_history began 2026-06-03 or by rows not in history); do not quote as a rate.' -- R1 Table D caveat, cited verbatim by contract CT-006 as '(R1 Table D caveat)'). The task text's own phrasing ('mismatched populations such as "18 of 31" are rejected') is this exact caveat.
_note: None of these atm_id values exist in the real docs/workable_items.db (verified 2026-09-29 by control needle #1 in test_reopen_rate_red.sh). The mismatch mechanic reproduced here: MB-004 has a Reopened event inside the window but ZERO closure events (Fixed/Implemented/Completed) anywhere in its ENTIRE history -- exactly R1's 'closed before item_history began, or by rows not in history' case. A naive tool that counts EVERY Reopened-in-window event as a numerator hit, without first checking the reopened item is ITSELF a member of the closed-in-window denominator population, produces reopened=1 (MB-004) / closed=3 (MB-001..MB-003) = 0.333... -- the exact '18 of 31'-shaped defect: a ratio of two counts drawn from two DIFFERENT underlying item sets, presented as if it were one rate.

item_history._note: THE MISMATCH ITEM: this is the ONLY item_history row of type Opened for MB-004 -- there is deliberately NO Fixed/Implemented/Completed row for MB-004 anywhere in this fixture (models R1's 'closed before item_history began, or by rows not in history'). MB-004 is therefore NOT a member of Bug's closed_in_window population.
Task type is CLEAN in this fixture -- included to prove refusal is scoped to the Bug type actually affected by the mismatch, not a global failure.
Feature type is also CLEAN in this fixture, for the same reason as MT-001.

Bug.closed_in_window_reasoning: Each of MB-001, MB-002, MB-003 has exactly one closure event (Fixed) with on_date inside [2026-07-01, 2026-07-31]. MB-004 has NO closure event of any kind anywhere in its history -- it is NOT a member of this population, regardless of its Reopened event's on_date.
Bug.naive_buggy_reopened_reasoning: A tool that queries 'distinct items with a Reopened event whose on_date is in the window' WITHOUT intersecting that result against closed_in_window would count MB-004 (Reopened on_date=2026-07-15, inside the window) -- but MB-004 is not a closed-in-window Bug, so this count is drawn from a DIFFERENT population than the closed=3 denominator.
Bug.naive_buggy_rate_reasoning: 1 (naive reopened, includes MB-004) / 3 (closed, excludes MB-004) = 0.333... -- structurally identical to R1's '18 of 31' (18 = whole-history reopened Bug items ever; 31 = whole-history closed Bug items ever; the two counts are NOT drawn from the same underlying set of item_history rows). This value MUST NEVER appear in reopen_rate.py's real output for this fixture.
Bug.correct_reopened_reasoning: The CORRECT reopened-in-window count, restricted to members of closed_in_window (per T-D06's own text: 'both counted from the same population (items closed within the window)'), is 0 -- none of MB-001, MB-002, MB-003 has a Reopened event at all.
Bug.mismatched_items_reasoning: MB-004 has a Reopened event inside the window but zero closure events anywhere in its history -- this is precisely the ambiguity the R1 Table D caveat names. reopen_rate.py MUST detect this and refuse to emit ANY numeric rate for Bug in this window, citing the mismatch and naming MB-004, rather than silently either (a) including MB-004 in the numerator against a denominator that excludes it (the naive-buggy 0.333... above), or (b) silently dropping MB-004 and reporting the correct-looking-but-unflagged 0/3=0.0 as if nothing were wrong (which would hide a real data-quality gap from the SC-004 metric consumer -- CT-006 requires the REFUSAL to be visible, not a silently-adjusted clean number).

Task.rate_reasoning: Clean, matched population -- no mismatch mechanic present for Task in this fixture.

Feature.rate_reasoning: Clean, matched population -- no mismatch mechanic present for Feature in this fixture.

overall.overall_reasoning: Because the Bug type's own population is mismatched/ambiguous, the OVERALL aggregate rate (which would otherwise sum closed/reopened across all three types) MUST ALSO refuse rather than silently aggregate a type it cannot safely count -- an overall rate that quietly excluded the ambiguous type, or quietly included the naive-buggy Bug numerator, would itself be exactly the kind of silent population-mismatch CT-006 forbids at the top level, one layer up from the per-type case.
